mainTopic: Unintended benefit from forbidden things (פרה אדומה, אבידה, כלאים), and an oven heated with forbidden fuel (זה וזה גורם)
overview: This amud finishes the debate between אביי and רבא about benefit a person does not intend. First the גמרא sets aside the case of the threshing פרה אדומה: a bird resting on the פרה leaves it valid, but a male animal mounting it makes it invalid. רב פפא explains from the כתיב (עָבַד) and the קרי (עֻבַּד) of the פסוק that work disqualifies the animal only when the owner is pleased with it. A proof from a lost object (אבידה) that may not be spread out in front of guests is rejected, because there the worry is damage from an evil eye or thieves. Then the משנה about merchants carrying כלאים garments shows that avoidable but unintended benefit is permitted, and the first version of רבא is refuted. The גמרא next turns to the משנה's words about heating an oven, and brings a ברייתא: an oven heated with ערלה or כלאי הכרם fuel must be smashed if new and cooled if old. רבי forbids bread baked in it and חכמים permit it. A contradicting ברייתא is first explained as רבי versus רבנן. That answer is rejected and replaced with רבי אליעזר versus רבנן, based on the rule of זה וזה גורם. The search for which ruling of רבי אליעזר is meant, starting with his ruling about leaven, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The threshing heifer only compares to the bird and the male animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the previous challenge. The פרה אדומה that threshed in the stall should be compared to two other cases. A bird landing on the פרה does not disqualify it. A male animal mounting it does disqualify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case is only like that case: if a bird rested on the heifer, it is still valid. If a male animal mounted it, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the previous challenge about the פרה אדומה that threshed. It says the case belongs with a separate pair of פרה rules: a bird landing on it and a male animal mounting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of פרה אדומה are measured by a special test that belongs only to פרה, not by the general rules of unavoidable benefit. A bird resting on the פרה does not disqualify it. A male animal mounting it does disqualify it. So the threshing case cannot serve as a general proof in the debate.

keyTerms.meaning: This is only comparable to that
Red heifer, which becomes invalid if work is done with it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a bird landing on the פרה counts as 'work' while the male animal does not. Physically, both are just something resting on the animal. The difference is about the owner's interest, which the next steps will explain.

phrases.english: This is comparable only to that:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is saying the earlier case should really be compared to a different one.

phrases.english: If a bird rested on it, it is valid,
If a male animal mounted it, it is invalid.
phrases.notes: The owner generally wants his cow to be bred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the threshing פרה that came on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-categorization: the case is moved into a special פרה framework instead of the general benefit debate.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The threshing פרה could serve as proof about unavoidable benefit in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: The threshing פרה belongs with the bird and male-animal rules of פרה אדומה, which follow their own test.

steps.title: Why is the bird different from the male animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the difference between a bird and a male animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a bird does not disqualify the פרה but a male animal does. This question sets up רב פפא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the פרה did nothing on purpose, and the owner did not make it happen. So the גמרא needs a principle that explains why one case disqualifies and the other does not.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the distinction in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and logic for why a male animal disqualifies the פרה but a bird does not.

steps.title: רב פפא: what each reading alone would mean
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא lays out two possibilities. If the פסוק were written and read as עָבַד ('he worked'), only work the owner himself did would disqualify. If it were written and read as עֻבַּד ('it was worked'), even work that happened on its own would disqualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If it were written עָבַד (he worked) and read עָבַד, the heifer would be invalid only once the owner himself worked it. If it were written עֻבַּד (it was worked) and read עֻבַּד, it would be invalid even if the work happened by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא starts answering by imagining two other ways the פסוק could have been written. Each one alone would give an extreme rule. This sets up his real conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים (21:3) is about the עגלה ערופה, a heifer אשר לא עֻבַּד בה, and the same rule about work is applied to the פרה אדומה. The spelling allows the word to be read as עָבַד, which would limit disqualification to the owner's own action. The vocalized reading עֻבַּד would extend it to any work at all, even work that happened on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written: the spelling of the word in the text (כתיב)

steps.confusionAlert: These two cases are hypothetical. The פסוק is not actually written and read the same way in either version. רב פפא is showing what each version alone would teach, so that he can combine them in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If it were written 'he worked' and we read 'he worked,'
phrases.notes: Just imagining here: both the spelling and the reading would mean someone did the work himself.

phrases.english: [it would not be invalid] until he himself works with it.
If it were written 'it was worked' and we read 'it was worked,'
phrases.notes: Just imagining here: both the spelling and the reading would mean the work was done to it.

phrases.english: even [work that happened] by itself would also [disqualify].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אִי כְּתִיב ״עָבַד״ וְקָרֵינַן ״עָבַד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 2 by analyzing the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer depends on the כתיב/קרי of the word in the פסוק. Here he sets out the two extreme readings.

steps.title: Combining the written and read forms: work the owner is pleased with
steps.stepSummary: Since the word is written עָבַד but read עֻבַּד, the two are combined. Work that happens to the פרה disqualifies it only if it resembles the owner's own work, meaning work he is pleased with.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that it is written 'he worked' and read 'it was worked': 'it was worked' is like 'he worked.' Just as 'he worked' means work he is pleased with, so too 'it was worked' means work he is pleased with.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his conclusion. The פרה becomes invalid even from work that happened on its own, but only if the owner is pleased with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרי (עֻבַּד) teaches that the owner does not have to do the work himself. The כתיב (עָבַד) teaches that the work must still resemble his own action, meaning he must be pleased with it. A bird gives the owner nothing, so the פרה stays valid. Breeding by a male is something the owner wants, so the פרה becomes invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (that the actual situation is so)
He is pleased with it, it benefits him
Just as ... so too (a comparison formula)

steps.whatToRemember: For פרה אדומה, work disqualifies the פרה even if the owner did not do it, but only when he is pleased with it (ניחא ליה). This is why a bird does not disqualify it but a male animal does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the answer in step 1. The פרה cases follow a special test of ניחא ליה drawn from the פסוק, so they cannot decide the general debate between אביי and רבא about unavoidable benefit.

phrases.english: Now that it is written 'he worked' and we read 'it was worked,'
'it was worked' is like 'he worked.'
Just as 'he worked' is something he is pleased with,
so too 'it was worked' [disqualifies only when] he is pleased with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two hypothetical readings from step 3 into the actual rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Work disqualifies the פרה when it happens in a way the owner is pleased with. A bird gives him no benefit, but breeding does.

steps.title: New proof from spreading out a lost object when guests come
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a lost object (אבידה). The finder may not spread it out for his own use. He may spread it out for the object's sake. But if guests are present, he may not spread it out at all, even for the object's sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A lost object: he may not spread it out on a bed or on a frame for his own needs. But he may spread it out for its needs on a bed or a frame. If guests happened to come to him, he may not spread it out on a bed or a frame, neither for its needs nor for his needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source into the debate about unavoidable benefit. It is a ברייתא about a finder airing out a lost object while guests are present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With guests present, the finder cannot air the object without displaying it, and he also enjoys showing it off, so the benefit is both unavoidable and intended. Since the ברייתא forbids it even for the object's sake, this seems to support רבא's view that such benefit is forbidden. The next step rejects this proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source as proof or challenge)
A lost object held by the finder
A frame or rack for hanging or airing items
For his own needs / for its (the object's) needs

steps.confusionAlert: The ban when guests are present applies even 'for its needs.' Normally airing it for its needs is allowed. The guests change the case because the finder now automatically gets the benefit of displaying the object.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A lost object: he may not spread it out
neither on a bed
nor on a frame for his own needs,
phrases.notes: Using someone else's item for oneself is forbidden.

phrases.english: but he may spread it out for its needs
phrases.notes: For example, to air it so it does not spoil.

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי מִטָּה וְעַל גַּבֵּי מַגּוֹד.
phrases.english: on a bed or on a frame.
If guests happened to come to him,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִשְׁטָחֶנָּה לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי מִטָּה
phrases.english: he may not spread it out, neither on a bed
nor on a frame,
whether for its needs or for his needs.
phrases.notes: Even doing it for the item's sake is forbidden here, because he automatically gets to show it off to the guests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the פרה case was set aside as a special rule, the גמרא brings a new source for the general debate.
steps.raayaObject: The view (רבא) that benefit which cannot be avoided but which one does intend is still forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a lost object: when guests are present, spreading it out is forbidden even for the object's own sake.

steps.title: The lost-object case is forbidden because of possible damage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the אבידה case. With guests present, spreading out the object is forbidden only because it might be damaged, by an evil eye or by thieves.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because he is damaging it, either because of the evil eye or because of thieves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the lost-object ברייתא. It says that case has a separate reason that has nothing to do with benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that spreading the object in front of guests was forbidden because of the benefit the finder gets. The גמרא answers that the real problem is risk to the object. Guests may cast an evil eye on it, or they may learn it is valuable and come back to steal it. So the case proves nothing about unintended benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there (a standard way of pushing away a proof)

phrases.english: It is different there
because he damages it,
phrases.notes: He puts the lost object at risk.

phrases.english: either because of the evil eye,
or because of thieves.
phrases.notes: The guests now know he has something valuable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the guest clause of the אבידה ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban there comes from danger to the object, not from the benefit.

steps.title: New proof from clothing merchants carrying כלאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about merchants selling כלאים garments. They may carry them in the normal way as long as they do not intend to be protected from sun or rain. The צנועין hang the garments on a stick behind them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Clothing merchants may sell in their usual way, as long as one does not intend to be protected from the sun in the sun, or from the rain in the rain. The modest ones hang them behind their backs on a stick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to test the question of unintended benefit. This step sets up the source, and the next step draws the inference from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Merchants drape the garments over their shoulders, so they do get some protection from sun and rain. The משנה allows this as long as they do not intend that protection. It also mentions that the צנועין avoid the benefit completely with a stick. That detail shows the benefit was clearly avoidable.

keyTerms.meaning: As long as he does not intend

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Clothing merchants sell in their usual way,
phrases.notes: They drape the כלאים garments over themselves.

phrases.english: as long as he does not intend
in the sun, for protection from the sun,
or in the rain, for protection from the rain.
And the modest ones hang them
behind their backs on a stick.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מוֹכְרֵי כְסוּת מוֹכְרִין כְּדַרְכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous proof is rejected, a new one is brought.
steps.raayaObject: Whether avoidable, unintended benefit is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כלאים about clothing merchants.

steps.title: The merchants could avoid the benefit, yet it is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the merchants could act like the צנועין and avoid the benefit. Even so, the משנה permits it when they have no intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here it is possible to act like the modest ones, and still, when he does not intend, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the inference from the merchant משנה. This is a case of benefit that could be avoided but is not intended, and it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stick method shows the benefit is avoidable (אפשר). The merchant does not want the benefit (לא קא מכוין). The משנה still permits it, which goes directly against anyone who forbids avoidable, unintended benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Where it is possible (to avoid the benefit)

phrases.english: But here, isn't it
possible to act like the modest ones,
and still, when he does not intend, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the source brought in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that avoidable, unintended benefit is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here the benefit is avoidable and unintended, and the משנה still permits it.

steps.title: The first version of רבא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a conclusive refutation of the first version of רבא's position, and it accepts the refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of the one who teaches the first version of רבא. It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the merchant משנה disproves the first version of רבא. The question is settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבא forbade benefit that was avoidable even without intent. The משנה permits exactly that case, so the first version cannot stand. Repeating the word תיובתא means the refutation is final.
steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows the view that if one does not intend the benefit, it is permitted, even when he could have avoided it.
steps.confusionAlert: Only the first version of רבא's statement is refuted. The second version agrees that avoidable, unintended benefit is permitted, so רבא himself is not refuted in that version.

phrases.english: A refutation of the one who teaches
the first version of Rava's statement,
It is a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא לְמַאן דְּמַתְנֵי לִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the result of the challenge in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Avoidable but unintended benefit is permitted. The first version of רבא is rejected.

steps.title: An oven heated with forbidden fuel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line that one may not heat an oven with חמץ. It brings a ברייתא: an oven heated with ערלה peels or כלאי הכרם straw must be broken if new, and cooled if old.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he may not heat with it, etc.' The Rabbis taught: An oven that was heated with peels of ערלה or with straw of כלאי הכרם — if new, it must be broken; if old, it must be cooled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next words of our משנה. It then brings a ברייתא about an oven heated with forbidden fuel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new oven is hardened by its first firing, so the forbidden fuel has permanently improved it. That is why it must be smashed. An old oven gains only the current heat, so it is enough to let it cool before using it.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree in its first three years, forbidden for benefit
Forbidden mixed planting in a vineyard, forbidden for benefit

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how to deal with a benefit from a forbidden item that becomes built into an object, compared to a benefit that only lasts for now. The same idea applies to heating an oven with חמץ.

phrases.english: 'And he may not heat with it, etc.'
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה about חמץ.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
An oven that one heated
with peels of orlah fruit
or with straw of mixed vineyard plantings,
if new, it must be smashed,
if old, it must be cooled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יַסִּיק בּוֹ וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of unintended benefit and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new oven heated with fuel forbidden for benefit must be smashed. An old one must be cooled.

steps.title: The bread baked in the forbidden-fuel oven
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. If bread was baked in the oven, רבי forbids it and חכמים permit it. If it was cooked on the coals, everyone permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he baked bread in that oven, רבי says the bread is forbidden, and the חכמים say the bread is permitted. If he cooked it on top of the coals, everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא from the last step. Now it tells us what happens to bread that was baked in an oven heated with forbidden fuel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי forbids the bread because the forbidden fuel's heat helped bake it. The חכמים permit it. When the bread is cooked on coals, the forbidden wood has already burned down to coals, so everyone permits it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement between רבי and חכמים here becomes the first tool the גמרא uses to explain the contradiction in the next steps.

phrases.english: If he baked bread in it,
Rabbi says: the bread is forbidden,
and the Sages say: the bread is permitted.
If he cooked it on top of the coals —
phrases.notes: Here only coals are left from the forbidden fuel.

phrases.english: everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread baked in the oven: רבי forbids it and חכמים permit it. Bread cooked on the coals is permitted by everyone.

steps.title: Another teaching says every oven only needs cooling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא. It says an oven, whether new or old, only needs to be cooled. This contradicts the rule that a new oven must be broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: whether new or old, it should be cooled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from step 10 with a different ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said a new oven must be broken and an old oven only cooled. The second ברייתא says even a new oven only needs cooling. So the two teachings contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught (introduces a contradicting ברייתא)

phrases.english: But was it not taught:
whether new or old, it should be cooled!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a contradicting ברייתא against the one just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 10 that a new oven must be broken.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא says cooling is enough even for a new oven, which contradicts the first ברייתא.

steps.title: One teaching follows רבי, the other follows רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the strict ברייתא follows רבי and the lenient one follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one follows רבי, and that one follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. It says the two ברייתות simply follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי forbids bread baked with forbidden heat, so a new oven, which still holds that strength, must be broken. רבנן permit such bread, so cooling the oven is enough.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is Rabbi, and that one is the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two ברייתות follow different תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to follow one opinion and to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The breaking ברייתא follows רבי, and the cooling ברייתא follows רבנן.

steps.title: רבי's reason may not reach a case with two causes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer. רבי forbids the bread because the wood's benefit is in it. Future baking in the oven, though, comes from both forbidden and permitted causes (זה וזה גורם). We never heard רבי forbid that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that you heard רבי rule this way because the improvement from the wood is in the bread. But where 'this and that cause it,' did you hear him say so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. It shows that רבי's reason does not clearly lead to breaking a new oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי's case, the forbidden fuel alone baked the bread. Breaking an oven is about future baking, which will be heated by new, permitted wood together with the forbidden fuel's leftover strength. That is a case of זה וזה גורם, and רבי's ruling does not show that he forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: the improvement that comes from the wood
this and that both cause it (a forbidden and a permitted cause together)
did you hear him say so?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. The bread case is about bread already baked with only forbidden heat. Breaking the oven is about the future, when permitted wood will also be used.

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi rule this way
because there is improvement from the wood in the bread.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מִי שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Where this and that cause it — did you hear him say so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the breaking ברייתא follows רבי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי's case has only a forbidden cause. Breaking the oven involves both a forbidden and a permitted cause, and רבי never ruled on that.

steps.title: The strict teaching follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. The breaking ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who forbids זה וזה גורם. The cooling ברייתא follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult: this one follows רבי אליעזר, and that one follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first answer and gives a new one, tied to the rule of זה וזה גורם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that something is forbidden even when a permitted cause helped produce it. So a new oven must be broken, since future bread will be baked partly with forbidden strength. רבנן disagree, so cooling is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא who holds that זה וזה גורם is forbidden

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this one is Rabbi Eliezer, that one is the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two ברייתות follow different תנאים, now based on the rule of זה וזה גורם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who forbids זה וזה גורם.

steps.title: Which ruling of רבי אליעזר is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that רבי אליעזר forbids זה וזה גורם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the new answer. It is setting up a search for the right statement of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 assumed that רבי אליעזר forbids זה וזה גורם. Now the גמרא wants to find the specific teaching where he says this.

phrases.english: Which Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the answer in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which statement of רבי אליעזר shows that he forbids זה וזה גורם.

steps.title: A first suggestion: רבי אליעזר's ruling about leaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the source is the משנה about חולין leaven and תרומה leaven that fall into dough together. רבי אליעזר says 'I follow the last one.' חכמים say it is never forbidden, whichever fell first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is רבי אליעזר about leaven, as we learned: חולין leaven and תרומה leaven fell into dough. Neither one alone was enough to make it rise, but together they made it rise. רבי אליעזר says: I follow the last one. The חכמים say: whether the forbidden one fell in first or last, it never makes the dough forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible source for רבי אליעזר's view. It opens with 'אילימא' ('if you say'), which signals that it is about to test this suggestion and may reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here two leavens, one permitted and one forbidden, work together to make the dough rise. That is a case of זה וזה גורם. רבי אליעזר rules by whichever fell in last, so if the תרומה fell last, the dough is forbidden. חכמים never forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (opens a suggestion that may be rejected)
the portion given to a כהן, forbidden to others

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that רבי אליעזר does not say the dough is always forbidden. He follows whichever leaven fell in last. That detail is the reason the גמרא is checking whether this source really fits.

phrases.english: If you say it is Rabbi Eliezer about leaven,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
leaven of non-sacred food and of terumah
that fell into dough,
and this one is not enough to make it rise
and that one is not enough to make it rise,
but they combined and made it rise —

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַחַר אַחֲרוֹן אֲנִי בָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: I follow the last one,
and the Sages say:
whether the forbidden one fell in first,
or the forbidden one fell in last —
it never makes it forbidden
phrases.notes: The חכמים's sentence continues on the next amud with a qualification.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggestion that the source is רבי אליעזר's ruling about leaven, where he follows the last ingredient that fell in.
